policies.title: Audit rules are not locked (-e 2)
policies.description: Checks that the final rule enables immutable mode.
policies.rationale: An attacker with root could otherwise switch auditing off without a reboot.
policies.absence_note: Without -e 2 the rules can be changed at runtime: treated as a failure.
policies.remediation: Put -e 2 as the last line (note: changes then need a reboot).
references: Linux audit subsystem rule syntax (auditctl/audit.rules, public)

policies.title: Not audited: changes to /etc/passwd
policies.description: Checks that this rules file audits changes to /etc/passwd.
policies.rationale: Account additions are a common persistence step.
policies.absence_note: A rules file is assessed on its own: absence means this file does not audit it (it may be audited in another rules.d file, which is not visible): treated as a failure.
policies.remediation: Add a matching audit rule (for example -w <path> -p wa -k <tag>, or an -a syscall rule).
references: Linux audit subsystem rule syntax (auditctl/audit.rules, public)
